Executive summary

In two weeks, Oracle went from “analysis of a sample” to “counting everyone, and seeing why”

It counts everyone

8,119 first payers, 38.3M purchase attempts, 104K churned players. Answers computed on Nexon’s actual populations.

It sees the why

The actual screens behind the numbers. The popup right before a first payment, the boss fight before a churn, the error dialog behind a failed purchase.

It checks the data too

Telemetry and schema issues discovered during analysis, packaged so the data team can verify and act on them directly.

How it works

Every answer starts from Nexon’s data and ends on an actual screen

1
Nexon warehouse · quantitative

Count everyone

Full-population computation on the tables and definitions Nexon’s data team built. Revenue, payments, churn segments, loyalty, predicted LTV, with “this is your population” stated on the result.

2
Recorded gameplay · qualitative

See the reason

Replays actual sessions from the cohort stage 1 identified, to confirm the on-screen cause. Error dialogs, offer popups, chat, UI friction. The layer that never lands in a log.

Every question in the pilot was handled in natural language. Table selection, query writing, validation. At no point did an analyst touch the warehouse directly.

Findings

Category reports

Report 01

Chat moderation

The same money-selling advert running untouched on four servers. A filter that blocks “palabok” and “Buccees” without saying why, then lets a spaced-out slur through. Players report spam and give up on abuse. None of it exists in the warehouse.

Open the report →
Report 02

Retention and churn

Where new players stall in the first hour, and what fills the last minutes before they stop. Each moment seen on a real recording.

Open the report →
Report 03

Technical issues and UX friction

Eight issues on screen: a live store bug, a purchase that succeeds without telling the player, ad errors that report the wrong reason, and a session crash landing right after a boss failure.

Open the report →
Next step

Post-pilot: SDK integration unlocks deeper game intelligence

The pilot read gameplay from the outside. With the SDK, gameplay, events and screen data come together, unlocking richer insights and faster action.

A/B testing

See what players actually do Go beyond conversion rates to see how players respond to a change, whether they notice it, engage with it, or ignore it.

Journey mapping

See the complete player journey Connect player actions, events and gameplay on one timeline to understand where players drop off, get stuck or convert.

Tutorial analysis

Find exactly where players get stuck See which steps cause friction, how long players spend there, and whether the guidance helps them move forward.

Deeper player insight

Understand the why behind player behaviour Connect what players do with what they see and experience to understand their intent, friction and decisions.
